title: Ten weeks of evenings: what a course is really like
excerpt: Two evenings a week after a full day of work is a real commitment. A week-by-week account from someone who has just finished.
content:
Two evenings a week after a full day of work is a real commitment. We asked Mira, who finished the web development course in December, to describe how the ten weeks actually felt.

Weeks one to three: everything is new

“I went home with a headache the first night. By week three I had a page with my name on it, online, and I showed it to everyone at work.”

Weeks four to seven: the dip

“JavaScript nearly finished me. What helped was that the group was small enough for Samuel to notice, and that everyone else was stuck in the same place.”

Nobody tells you the middle is the hard part. It is, and then it is over.

Weeks eight to ten: your own project

“I built a booking page for my sister's salon. It is not perfect and it is in use, which is more than I can say for most things I have started.”
